essence: Twenty when-questions that are really one: when will longing become meeting?

It asks it of the mind (1), the face (2), needlessness (3), the gods (4), distinction (5), the slow (6), flight (7), the world (8), knowledge and yoga (9), all hearers (10), transparency (11), leadership (12), pride (13), lying down (14), the far shore (15), tears (16), beast-life (17), play (18), speech (19) — and answers it once, in the last verse: by hugging hard and seeing without effort (20).

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as the victory of autonomy
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of longing (utsuka); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the twentyfold kadā that never leaves Him. The rasa is the tranquility of autonomy — freedom desiring only itself; the victory is that the questions never leave Him. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as the sole object of longing.
